lesson_title: The Right Stuff for the Job
hook_text: Would you make a raincoat out of a towel? Then why do we make towels out of cotton?
clip_script: Testing lab in rainy George! Scratch it: stone and metal are hard, foam is soft. Bend it: wood is stiff, rubber is flexible. Hang weights on it: paper tears, rope holds. Weigh it: same size, but the metal block is heaviest. Drip water on it: plastic is waterproof, cotton soaks it up. So, a raincoat from cotton? Soggy! A towel from plastic? Useless! Choose the right properties for the job.
visual_style: Whiteboard testing table with five pairs of words; materials get scratched, bent, pulled, weighed and dripped on, then sorted into the right job.
mood: Like a testing lab where learners are the scientists.
pacing: Five quick tests, one per pair of properties, then a match-the-job round.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and test three materials at home for waterproof or absorbent.
